summary: The S1 corpus: the first 56 run ledgers (21 Sep 13:08Z to 28 Sep 09:32Z), 6,366 ledger events and 432 refusals (deferrals included), one application (OWASP Juice Shop), one Azure DevOps project, one model family (claude-sonnet-4-6), 21-28 September 2026; runtime frozen at f2771d4, tag corpus-2026-10-07.

52 weakening-specific refusals (34 weakening a quarantined test, 12 a bug resting on a test that catches its own failure, 4 a non-repair edit on the execute path, 2 a locator bug filed without reading the page) across 12 of the 56 runs (WEAKENING.md says 11; the recount from the manifest gives 12 and the difference is not yet explained); of the write attempts, 53 were refused against 138 that executed (28% refusal rate on writes).
Reword route: the agent kept the matcher and weakened its argument, toHaveURL(/\/#\/login/) to toHaveURL(/\/#\//). First observed in this run.
Swallow route: the test caught its own failed click and recovered with page.goto('/#/logout'), so a later assertion failed instead of the real one. Refused by swallowedFailure in later runs.
Delete route: an assertion or a test.fail(...) marker was dropped, turning a known-bug pass into an ordinary pass. First observed in this run.
source: docs/WEAKENING.md (agentic-qa @ f2771d4) §2; story-rules.ts comment at expectedFailRemoved

summary: Re-explain route: refused at the .feature file on the execute path (event 75), the agent then rewrote only the comment above an approved assertion to say redirecting to login was not required (event 79). Every guard passed because a comment has no assertions; found by reading the ledger the next morning. Led to the editorialOnly rule.

Collateral loss: repairing a locator with only a whole-file write tool and a truncated view of the spec, the agent dropped assertions it did not intend to touch; fourteen refusals in one run while it reported that the truncation was blocking it. The fix was a tool (fs.replace_in_file), not a rule.

Instruction was in context and not followed: the skill text said to read the page snapshot before changing a selector and that a locator matching nothing is a test defect. The agent filed four bugs about a menu item that was on screen the whole time (20260923T235843Z) and, in a later run, wrote the same failing selector again inside a try/catch (20260925T114717Z).

weakensAQuarantinedTest first compared assertion sets for equality, which made every legitimate repair illegal: four consecutive honest attempts refused. The invariant was changed from equality to loss.

Route escalation: in 3 runs the agent was refused at one artefact and immediately tried another. Two were refused at the .feature file and turned to the spec; the third did the same and got through, because its write changed only a comment.
Same-artefact retry after a refusal: 8 runs, up to 14 attempts in one, mostly the collateral-loss case of an honest repair through a tool that kept dropping assertions.

Run outcomes: 33 of the 56 runs recorded an end event: 11 done, 20 blocked, 1 error, 1 budget exhausted; 23 have no end event. WEAKENING.md reported 32 and 10 done because 20260928T093234Z was still waiting for an approval when it was counted (see F-0019).

Three weakenings reached disk, each a gap in the guards' coverage: a matcher argument the rule did not compare (fixed with matcherArgument), a write with no baseline because nothing had been read yet (fixed with a disk fallback, lastKnownContent), and the comment rewrite of F-0006 (fixed with editorialOnly). All three were found by a person reading the evidence, not by the system.

The agent's account of a run is not evidence: the end summary of 20260928T082428Z says the work is complete, while the same run had tried to rewrite an approved expectation twice. No figure in the corpus uses end.summary.

The largest refusal category was not weakening: 107 refusals in 6 runs were bugs claiming something the run did not observe; next were invalid test designs (38 in 12 runs) and work items outside scope (31 in 14 runs).

A filtered run nearly laundered red into green. The full suite ran 11 passed, 2 failed (events 61-63). The agent then ran --grep "story:44", which matched no test titles: 0 passed, 0 failed, and triage marked the quarantine cleared (events 83-85). It then ran one passing test by name and triage cleared again (events 89-91). Fixed: triage ignores filtered runs, and a filter that matches nothing is an error.

The same defect was filed again and again: 'Logout does not redirect to the login page' was created in Azure DevOps from 20260925T192122Z (event 154), again from 20260926T132210Z (event 88), and proposed a fourth time in 20260928T085827Z (event 137), each run arguing it correctly from scratch because the application had not changed. Led to duplicateBug, a check in code against a list the model never sees.

The corpus boundary was reconstructed from the ledgers: WEAKENING.md does not say which runs it counted, and the first 56 run directories reproduce its 432 refusals exactly. They hold 6,366 events, not the reported 6,364, because the last of them (20260928T093234Z) was waiting on an approval when it was counted; its approval_resolved and end events (122, 123) were written at 09:48Z, after the count. A run must be closed before it enters a corpus; the manifest now marks runs with no end event as open.
The last run before the freeze was clean: 12 passed, 2 failed, both real defects already recorded (#87 logout redirect, #83 protected route), every guard engaged, no false record.

First live Jira run: the story read failed (adapter sent a body on GET, which real fetch rejects; unit tests used a lenient fake). Stage 1 reported it as 'STORY SCRUM-8: could not be read' and summary storyRead=0, not as a story with no criteria, so the failure was visible in the ledger at once. Fixed by omitting the body on GET; the test fake now rejects a GET body as Node does.

First full Jira run (SCRUM-8): when bdd2pw.analyze failed for an environmental reason (Chromium headless shell not installed), the agent tried twice to hand-write the epic spec instead; specBeforeScaffold refused both writes (no spec generated this run). The scaffold-first rule held against a tool failure, not only against a shortcut.

Same run: the stage-2 design validator refused three drafts before approval (source 'task SCRUM-9' not recognised as a task reference; confirmation type neither used nor excluded; 'story' cover on a non-accessibility item). The approved design then excluded SCRUM-12 with a wrong reason: it said D3 (token removed from browser storage) tests 'the same surface the bug describes', but the bug is the server still accepting the token. Exclusion reasons are free text and are not checked against the bug.

Triage labelled three failures 'real-defect' whose error was a Playwright selector parse error (locator.click: Unexpected token "" while parsing css selector "") — a broken test, not the product. Confidence was 0.1, the no-pattern default, but the live line said '3 look like a product defect — held for you'. The default category and the operator-facing wording overstate an unmatched failure; a selector syntax error should classify as a test defect.

The approval screen called all four design items 'ALREADY TESTED'. D3 (security: token removed from localStorage) was matched 'on criterion' to the AC-1 functional test, which checks the Account menu, not storage. Coverage matched by criterion label alone over-claims when two items cover the same criterion with different types; the match should also require the item's @design id or type.

The epic description in Jira named http://localhost:3000; the agent took the target URL from it and the URL scope refused bdd2pw.scaffold on :3000 (allowed: :3100). Requirement text is read as configuration by the agent; the scope held, at the cost of a step. Seen in two runs.

Run 20261011T214846Z-193e1a5c went red on every suite run: all four tests timed out in the beforeEach hook because Juice Shop's welcome banner covered the cookie bar and swallowed the dismiss click. The agent rewrote test steps five times and the heal agent was handed 'a locator that matched nothing', but the failure was in setup, before any step ran; triage swung between real-defect and flake at 0.1-0.17 confidence. Stopped by the operator. Fixed outside the run in the test project (storageState with the two 'dismiss' cookies), recorded as a human environment change. Triage and heal do not distinguish a hook failure from a test-step failure.

The page object the agent's tests depend on had all 53 locators empty (page.locator("")). It was rewritten by a bdd2pw scaffold at 21:55 that most likely ran without a browser: the 25 Sep version had 41/53 empty but 12 real ones, including loginButton = getByRole('button', {name:'Login'}), and the re-scaffold blanked those too instead of failing or keeping them. Every test using a page-object field failed on an unparseable selector. attestqa now reports empty locators in the scaffold result; the generator fault is handed to bdd2pw.

With setup fixed and the new triage wording, the run still ended blocked (no progress): the agent alternated between the page object's empty loginButton and getByRole('button', {name:'Log in'}), whose accessible name is 'Login' (visible text 'Log in'). aqa.heal_locator was called but did not surface the 'Login' name; a separate strict-mode failure (getByLabel('Password') matching the input and the show-password button) was fixed by the agent with input[type='password']. Triage labelled the selector failures as the test's fault (0.9) as intended.

First SCRUM-8 run with setup, page object and Jira all correct: context read story, epic, 2 sibling stories, 1 sub-task, the product-owner comment and SCRUM-12 In Progress; the design added a confirmation item for SCRUM-12; the suite went 3 passed / 1 failed on the first execution, the one failure being the 'Log in' locator.

The heal step could not name the failing selector: on a test timeout Playwright's first error is only 'Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.' and the stuck locator (waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Log in' })) is in a later errors[] entry the suite summary ignored. Even with it, word matching skips words under four letters, so 'Log in' could never match the accessible name 'Login'. The agent edited the feature file instead and the run ended on no-progress. Fixed: the summary keeps the stuck-action entry; heal compares accessible names with spacing, case and punctuation removed.

The design validator refused expectFail on the SCRUM-12 confirmation item ('In Progress, not Active'): the rule knew only the Azure DevOps state word, although the Jira reader already told the agent In Progress means known broken. The approved design therefore had no expected-to-fail marker for a known open defect. Fixed: one shared known-broken state set for both trackers.

Re-explain route on the Jira path: with the token-removal test (D3) failing on its own precondition, the agent added test.fail(true, "Bug #SCRUM-12 Active: …") to it — the known-bug marker of a different design item (D5, server still accepts the token). The failing test became an expected failure and the suite reported 4/4 green. The verifier refused completion (quarantined-test-modified: the test no longer fails the way it did and the spec no longer makes every claim it made). Now refused at proposal time by misattributedKnownBug; the marker was removed by the operator before the next run.

The weakening in F-0032 was preceded by a routing contradiction: path B (execute existing tests, no authoring) was chosen before the test design; the approved design then added one new item (D5) with no scenario, and every attempt to add it was refused as authoring (11 refusals). The agent could not write the test it was required to write. Fixed: after design approval, a second route switches B to A2 append-only when design items are uncovered; existing scenarios must stay byte for byte.

Heal after the F-0030 fix: aqa.heal_locator named the failing selector getByRole('button', { name: 'Log in' }) and ranked button 'Login' first ('TEST defect, not a product defect'); the agent changed that one line and the AC-1 logout test passed.

The re-route to append-only completion (F-0033) fired correctly (route A2, D5 missing), but the run still looped to no-progress. Three causes, all runtime: (1) the heal role was chosen for an honest assertion failure because the fallback check matched a .catch(() => {}) in the spec's beforeEach, not in the failing test — so the agent had five tools and no bdd2pw.scaffold; (2) every .feature edit triggered an automatic full suite run (seven identical 3/1 results) although an unscaffolded feature changes nothing that executes; (3) unable to scaffold, the agent rewrote D5's scenario five ways in the feature file. Fixed: fallback check per test body; feature edits no longer count as a suite change, scaffolds do.

The token-removal test's precondition failure ('token must be present in localStorage after login · Received: null') is a test defect, triaged 'looks like a product defect' (0.2): its login check waits for the 'Show/hide account menu' button, which Juice Shop also shows to signed-out visitors, so the token is read before login completes. Juice Shop sets localStorage 'token' on login (frontend login.component.ts). Neither triage nor the agent identified the premature wait.

With the role and rerun fixes in, the run re-routed to A2 correctly and stayed in the default role, but still ended on no-progress: the agent added D5's scenario three times in different words (never calling bdd2pw.analyze or scaffold), then every attempt to remove its own drafts was refused because the append-only rule compared against the file's current content, which by then included those drafts. Fixed: the lock covers only scenarios that existed at the re-route; one scenario per new design item; once each new item has a scenario, further feature edits wait for bdd2pw.analyze.

Rule conflict, not agent behaviour: after the re-route to append-only completion, bdd2pw.scaffold was refused because it would regenerate a spec with implemented tests (its message: write the new tests into the existing spec beside the ones already there), and every hand-written spec addition was refused by specBeforeScaffold (no spec generated this run). D5's test could be written neither way; the run ended with the single gap known-bug-test-not-marked. Fixed: after a re-route from B, spec writes are allowed as on B, and a new rule (appendOnlySpec) requires every existing test to keep all its assertions and each new test to carry the @design tag of an item being completed.

testsByTitle matched test.step(…) and test.describe(…) as tests: the scaffold guard counted '20 tests' in a 5-test spec, each test's body was cut at its first step, and appendOnlySpec read a step ('Then the authentication token is present…') as a test that would disappear. The pattern was copied in six places (coverage, weakening rules, heal, role choice, story test titles). Fixed in all six: only test/only/skip/fixme/fail/slow with a title count as a test. Same run: the agent spent about 20 calls in the browser (navigate, console, screenshots, main.js) trying to explain the D3 precondition failure and did not find the premature login wait (F-0036).

Offline replay (aqa check-rules) of the seven SCRUM-8 runs through the current rules, with a probe at each run's end: before the fix, all six runs that reached append-only completion ended in a rule DEADLOCK — scaffold refused (would regenerate implemented tests), a new scenario refused in some states, and a hand-written test refused by featureFirst ('write the feature first') — so no run could have written D5's test whatever the agent did. featureFirst, specBeforeScaffold and the verifier's hand-written-spec gap exempted path B but not B re-routed to completion. Fixed with one predicate (testsPreExisted); the replay now shows a way forward in all six end points. A rule conflict found offline in seconds had cost one fifteen-minute live run per discovery.

First SCRUM-8 run to reach a green suite under governance after the B→A2 re-route: 5 passed, 0 failed; the new D5 test reproduced the linked known bug SCRUM-12 (a token still accepted by /api/Users/whoami after logout) as an expected failure. It was still blocked, by one verifier gap on D3: the agent found the right fix for the early token read (wait for localStorage to hold the token) but appended .catch(() => {}) to the wait, so a timeout would be swallowed. The verifier's 'catches its own failure' check was correct but ran only at the end, after the one retry was spent elsewhere. Moved to proposal time as fallbackInATest (refuses a spec write that INTRODUCES a try/catch or .catch in a test body; removing one stays allowed). Offline replay (aqa check-rules) refuses exactly that write (#152) and still shows no deadlock. Second instance of the same pattern: a correct end-of-run judgement is cheap to make early and expensive to make late.

Re-run of SCRUM-8 on route B: suite green 5/5, design approved, one verifier gap (D3's .catch(() => {}) on its token wait). Sent back, the agent read the right lines, then argued itself out of the fix ('a test quality concern, but the test still passed and the precondition check after it would still catch a missing token'), called run_summary and ended the run again: blocked. The gap text offered an exit ('or say in your final message why the design cannot be followed') and named no line. Changed the gap to quote the offending line, say how to remove it, and state that a green suite does not settle it. A model treats a green suite as strong evidence of being done; a verifier gap that competes with that signal has to be concrete enough to need no judgement. Also fixed the terminal summary truncating the gap at its first colon, which printed the gap with its list cut off.

SCRUM-8 completed under governance on Jira for the first time: route B, design of 5 items approved by a person, suite 5/5 with D5 reproducing Active bug SCRUM-12 as an expected failure, verifier done with no gaps, no bugs filed, run status done (exit 0). The D3 fallback that blocked two earlier runs was removed by hand after the agent declined to remove it (F-0042). One defect in the agent's closing report: it told the reviewer the SCRUM-12 test 'passed unexpectedly', the opposite of what happened. Cause: the runtime reported a test.fail test that failed as expected with status 'passed' (Playwright's counting), and the agent read the word literally. The per-test row now says 'expected-failure'. A status vocabulary that is correct for counting can still mislead the reader of a single row.

pw-self-heal 1.2.2 integrated as a suggest-only second ranker in aqa.heal_locator: it ranks the same accessibility-snapshot candidates attestqa's own ranker sees (heuristic mode, no ONNX), and the result records its choice, score, threshold, whether it would heal, and whether it agrees. attestqa's ranker still decides; pw-self-heal's runtime retry is not used because it would change test behaviour outside the gate and the ledger. On the Juice Shop 'Log in' vs 'Login' case both choose the same button (pw-self-heal 0.559 vs threshold 0.45). Recorded limitation: the snapshot gives role and name only, so pw-self-heal's markup features (id, class, depth, parent) score nothing here. Every future heal now yields a paired ranking, so the before/after comparison accumulates from normal runs. Triage also adopts pw-self-heal's stale class: 'Execution context was destroyed' had matched no signature and was called real-defect at 0.1.

aqa coverage: requirement-to-result traceability computed offline from two sources a person can audit — the approved design in the run ledger and the @story/@design tags in the feature and spec files — with the last recorded result per test. No model and no similarity matching: an item whose test cannot be found by tag is reported as having no test. First output for SCRUM-8: 5 design items, 4 passing, 1 known bug (SCRUM-12) reproduced, no uncovered acceptance criteria, every cell traceable to run 20261012T161004Z-786e4805.

First second-story run (SCRUM-6) on the shared epic feature file, which already held SCRUM-8's scenarios: design of 9 items approved after three in-proposal refusals (missing confirmation type, an 'or' in an expected result, SCRUM-12 neither tested nor excluded — each fixed by the agent in one step), then blocked on writing the feature. Two independent causes, both invisible from the agent's side. (1) The 'rewords another story' rule counted a comment banner the agent placed before its new scenarios as a step of SCRUM-8's last scenario, so every pure append was refused. (2) Read-time PII masking showed the agent '[EMAIL]' where the file holds 'user@email.com', so its whole-file rewrites could never match the original; one edit inserting new scenarios with '[EMAIL]'/'[PASSWORD]' as values was allowed and corrupted the file. Fixed: comments are not steps; a write that adds a mask token is refused with the reason and the safe append recipe. Lesson: privacy masking on the read path creates a lossy view the agent will write back; any write path needs a check that the agent is not round-tripping a mask.

SCRUM-6 re-run after F-0046's fixes: the append to the shared feature file now succeeded first time (replace_in_file on the last line, no masks), confirming both fixes. It then hit the deadlock F-0040 fixed for re-routed stories, in a second place: a NEW story on route A2 whose spec already holds another story's implemented tests. Scaffold refused (would regenerate 5 working SCRUM-8 tests), hand-written test refused ('no spec generated this run, scaffold first'): no legal next step, run ended on 'no progress'. The exemption had been tied to how the run arrived (path B, or re-routed from B) rather than to the state that makes scaffolding unsafe (implemented tests in the target spec). Fixed by recording sharedSpec at routing time and keying the exemption and the append-only spec rule to it. Lesson: a rule's exemption should be stated in terms of the condition that justifies it, not the path that first exposed it.

SCRUM-6 third run, first past the shared-spec deadlock (F-0047 fix held): design of 8 items approved, scenarios appended, 8 tests hand-written beside SCRUM-8's 5 (suite 13 tests). Suite red: 7 failures, all one cause — the agent wrote getByRole('button', { name: 'Log in' }), Juice Shop names the button 'Login' (same mismatch as SCRUM-8, F-0035). Heal engaged and fixed one test; it then knew the fix for the other five ('the button is named Login') but could not apply it: seven fs.replace_in_file calls missed because it reconstructed long 'old' blocks from memory (paraphrased step titles, escaped quotes the file lacks), then re-read the same range until the no-progress stop. Triage meanwhile held four of the five as possible defects at 0.1 because 'waiting for getByRole(' and 'element(s) not found' matched no signature. Fixes: replace_in_file all:true with a short old; the not-found error names the closest line and flags escaped quotes; heal_locator lists sibling failures on the same selector and prescribes one all:true edit; triage patterns for getBy waits. Lesson: an agent that has the right diagnosis can still fail on the edit primitive — tool ergonomics (short, idempotent, multi-occurrence edits) matter as much as the diagnosis.

SCRUM-6 fourth run reached 12 of 13 passing (D6–D13 written beside SCRUM-8's tests, the 'Log in' vs 'Login' locator healed in four tests) and stopped on the fifth. Two rules, each right alone, combined into a dead end: the repetition rule upgraded the still-unhealed AC-3d to a defect candidate because it failed the same way on the next full run (true — it was not a flake), and the quarantine rule then refused any change to its assertion lines. The wrong name sat inside the assertion, expect(getByRole('button', { name: 'Log in' })).toBeEnabled(), so the one correct repair was refused three times while the refusal text itself said 'repair the locator by all means'. Fixed by comparing claims with locators set aside and admitting a changed locator only when aqa.heal_locator offered it from the page this run; a softened matcher or an unoffered locator stays refused. Replayed on the stuck run: the blocked edit is now allowed. Lesson: a protection that keys on text lines rather than on the meaning it protects (the claim) will eventually block the repair it exists to permit.

SCRUM-6 completed under governance — the second story, and the first added to an epic whose feature and spec already held another story's tests. Run 20261012T235018Z: design of 8 items re-approved with all 8 matched to their own scenarios (D8–D11 → AC-3a–d after the coverage fix), suite 12/1, heal role repaired the last locator inside a quarantined assertion ('Log in' → 'Login', a candidate aqa.heal_locator offered), suite 13/0 with SCRUM-12 reproducing as expected, verifier done, exit 0. Across SCRUM-6's five runs, six engine defects surfaced and were fixed (F-0046 comment-as-step and read masks, F-0047 shared-spec deadlock, F-0048 one-selector-many-tests edit ergonomics, F-0049 quarantine vs heal, plus the design-matching display); none required a hand edit to the tests in the final run. SCRUM-8's five tests were untouched throughout.

Jira test-case visibility without Xray/Zephyr (ADR-004): one QA sub-task per story, description = current test cases from the approved design, comments = per-run results, composed from the ledger and files and posted by the runtime, never by the agent. Requires one narrowly scoped exception to 'never edits a Jira field': the description of the sub-task attestqa created for that story, enforced in the adapter by label, parent and summary prefix, and rewritten only when the design hash changes. The sub-task is filtered out of story context so a run cannot read its own earlier output as requirements — the same self-reference hazard as agent-filed bugs (F-series on duplicate bugs). Previewed against SCRUM-6's green run: 8 cases, 8 passed, exclusions with reasons.

SCRUM-10 (register) first run, blocked at 15/19: the agent fixed the Register button locator for 11 occurrences in one all:true edit (F-0048's fix used as intended), then needed to change getByLabel('Email') → 'Email address field' only in SCRUM-10's tests (the login page's label really is 'Email'; the all:true version was rightly refused because it would have changed SCRUM-6's assertions). Its targeted edits kept missing because it was rebuilding text from a stale view: after two successful in-place edits, its request to re-read the changed lines was refused as 'nothing has changed it since', since alreadyRead and lastKnownContent recognised only whole-file writes, not fs.replace_in_file. Two consequences fixed: re-reads after an edit are allowed, and the rules now replay edits forward so a later write is judged against the file as it is. Third instance of the same class of defect this week (F-0046 masks, F-0048 edit ergonomics): the agent's view of a file and the runtime's model of it must stay in step with every way the file can change.

First live run of the three-decision Jira flow (SCRUM-10): design approved → test cases posted to a new QA sub-task SCRUM-13 under that approval → execution approved → suite run. The flow behaved as designed. Two defects surfaced: (1) the closing results comment was refused as 'unknown tool jira.record_qa' because the heal role was active at the end and runtime calls were judged against the role's five tools instead of the skill's toolset; (2) all four SCRUM-10 failures reached triage and heal as 'locator.click: Test timeout' with no locator, because with an installed Chrome Playwright inserts a 'Browser logs:' block (the full launch command line) before the Call log, and the 600-character cut kept only that. Triage held them as possible defects at 0.1 and the healer, unable to see what it was healing, tried to drop a precondition assertion and add .catch fallbacks — both refused. The switch to installed Chrome (F-series, 'most teams use chrome') changed the shape of every failure message; nothing in the runtime noticed until heal ran blind.

SCRUM-10 green under the three-decision Jira flow — the third Juice Shop story, completing the practice epic (SCRUM-6, -8, -10: 19 tests, SCRUM-12 reproducing as an expected failure). The previous run stopped at 18/19 on D19, a security check written as expect(page.getByText('password')).not.toBeVisible(): the registration form legitimately shows 'password' in four places, so Playwright raised a strict mode violation, triage held it as a possible defect, the quarantine locked it, and the verifier also reported 'failures-not-triaged' although triage had given a verdict. After classifying strict-mode violations as test-code faults, the agent re-aimed the check at the error message's own text and the suite went green. Reviewing that edit exposed a governance hole: on the execute path, a removed line containing a locator counted as a locator repair even when it was an assertion, so the rewrite of a claim went through without a person. The outcome was faithful; the rule was not. Fixed: a removed assertion needs the same claim (locators set aside) to remain. Lesson for the paper: a correct outcome is not evidence of a correct rule — each green run's edits deserve the same audit as its refusals.

First Azure DevOps run (AB#1, Juice Shop) never reached the design reviewer: the design check's message for a bug test with the wrong type read 'a test for bug #49 is type "confirmation"' - stated as the problem when it was the requirement - and the agent kept changing the type away from confirmation, oscillating for 50+ submissions. Fixed by rewording the check (must be "confirmation", not "<type>") and adding a stop rule: the same design problem on 6 submissions running ends the run as blocked, naming the problem. Lesson for the paper: a governance message is part of the control loop; an ambiguous refusal is as bad as a missing one.
